en: Itivuttaka 78 Tikanipāta, Third Chapter Thus it was said. This discourse was spoken by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute. “It is fitting for you, Ānanda, to speak thus. Therefore, Ānanda, listen and attend closely; I will speak. “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One then said this: “Ānanda, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three?

The person who is intent on the self, the person who is intent on others, and the person who is intent on both self and others. And how, Ānanda, is one a person intent on the self? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. Yet he does not attain the destruction of the taints in this very life, nor does he attain the final knowledge: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. But he attains the destruction of the taints after death, upon the breakup of the body. This, Ānanda, is called a person intent on the self. And how, Ānanda, is one a person intent on others? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells contemplating the body in the body... feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. Yet he does not attain the destruction of the taints in this very life, nor does he attain the final knowledge: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. But he attains the destruction of the taints after death, upon the breakup of the body. This, Ānanda, is called a person intent on others. And how, Ānanda, is one a person intent on both self and others? Here, Ānanda, a certain person dwells contemplating the body in the body... feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. And he attains the destruction of the taints in this very life, and he attains the final knowledge: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. This, Ānanda, is called a person intent on both self and others. These, Ānanda, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is marvelous, venerable sir! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: ‘There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. “Indeed, Ānanda, it is because I have known this as it really is, seen it as it really is, realized it as it really is, and penetrated it with wisdom, that I declare: ‘There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, the Venerable Ānanda delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus it was said. The Discourse on the Convergence of Elements.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Monks, it is according to their elements that beings converge and come together with other beings."
Beings of inferior disposition associate and come together with beings of inferior disposition;
beings of noble disposition associate and come together with beings of noble disposition.
Monks, even in the past, beings associated and came together with beings according to their respective elements.
Beings of inferior disposition associate and unite with beings of inferior disposition;
beings of noble disposition associate and unite with beings of noble disposition.
In the future too, monks, beings will associate and unite with beings according to their own elements.
Beings of inferior disposition will associate and come together with beings of inferior disposition;
beings of noble disposition will associate and come together with beings of noble disposition.
Even now, monks, in this present time, beings come together and unite with other beings according to their elements.
“Beings of inferior disposition associate and come together with beings of inferior disposition;
beings of noble disposition associate and come together with beings of noble disposition.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"The thicket of craving is born from association;
it is severed by non-association."
Just as one who has boarded a small raft might sink in the great ocean,
so too does one come to ruin by relying on the indolent.
Even one who lives rightly may fail;
therefore, one should avoid him—
the lazy person of inferior energy.
With noble ones who are secluded,
resolute, and meditative,
who are constantly possessed of aroused energy—
"One should dwell together with the wise.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The ninth [sutta].
